Rashi on Eruvin 64b:10:1.english: To the Ladder of Tyre - The ascents of a high mountain.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:13:1.hebrew: אבל יותר מרביעית כו' - וכיון דיין האיטלקי הוה ומשכר טפי, הוה ליה כיותר מרביעית:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:13:1.english: But more than a quarter-log, etc. - And since it was Italian wine, which is more intoxicating, it should be [considered] like more than a quarter-log.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:14:1.english: Riding is different - For he does not have the exertion of the journey.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:14:2.hebrew: לרמי בר אבא נמי - דאמר דרך מיל, והכא תני שלש מילין — לא תיקשי: דרכוב שאני, דאין לו טורח, ולפיכך אין מפיגו כל כך:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:14:2.english: According to Rami bar Abba as well - Who said [walking] the distance of a mil, and here it teaches three mil — [it] is not difficult: Riding is different, as he does not have exertion, and therefore it does not dispel it so much.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:16:1.english: It is [a dispute between] tanna’im - In Tractate Nedarim.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:16:2.hebrew: פותחין בחרטה - צריך לחכם למצוא פתח לשואל, שיהא לו פתחון פה לומר: "לדעת כן לא נדרתי, ואילו הייתי יודע שכן הוא, לא הייתי נודר", ונמצא נדר נעקר מאליו:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:16:2.english: One opens with regret - A sage must find an opening for the petitioner, so that he has grounds to say: "I did not vow with this in mind, and had I known that it was so, I would not have vowed"; and the vow is [thereby] found to be uprooted on its own.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:17:1.hebrew: אין פותחין - אין צריך לפתוח לו בחרטה, אלא החכם עוקרו אע"פ שאינו מוצא לו טעם עקירה. רבן גמליאל סבר כמאן דאמר פותחין, לפיכך הוצרך ישוב הדעת לחשב איזה פתח ימצא לו:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:17:1.english: One does not open - There is no need to open [an opening] for him through regret; rather, the Sage uproots it even though he does not find a reason for uprooting for him. Rabban Gamliel held in accordance with the one who says [that] one opens [an opening]; therefore, he required composure to consider what opening he would find for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:18:1.english: Whoever utters - One who takes a vow.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:18:2.hebrew: ראוי לדוקרו - דלמא לא מקיים ליה. והיינו פתח, דקאמר ליה: ״אילו היית יודע שאסור לנדור, וחייב מיתה אתה עליו, כלום היית נודר?״ ואמר ליה האיך: ״לא״:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:18:2.english: Deserves to be pierced - Lest he not fulfill it. And this was the opening, as he said to him: “Had you known that it is forbidden to vow, and that you are liable to death for it, would you have vowed at all?” And that man said to him: “No.”

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:18:3.english: Rather, the tongue of the wise heals - For they dissolve his vow for him.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:1:1.hebrew: בעל בנכסי אשתו - בעי למיעבד בהו מצוה, דמילתא דתווהו בה אינשי נמי היא, ושלטא בהו עינא בישא:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:1:1.english: A husband with his wife’s property - He needs to perform a mitzvah with them, for this, too, is a matter that people marvel at, and the evil eye has power over them.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:20:1.hebrew: פתיתין אין מעבירין עליהן - אלא נוטלין אותן, דליכא למיחש לכשפים:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:20:1.english: [Regarding] pieces [of bread], one does not pass by them - Rather, one picks them up, as there is no concern of witchcraft.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:20:2.english: And on pieces do they not perform - Witchcraft.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:20:3.hebrew: דשקלן באגרייהו - פתיתי לחם, לעשות כשפים מדברים אחרים. והכי קאמר נביא: בשביל פיתותי לחם שנותנים לכן בשכרכן, חיללתן את שמי בתוך עמי, שהייתן עושות בהן כשפים לנביאי הבעל, להטעות את עמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:20:3.english: That they took [them] as their wages - [Namely,] pieces of bread, [as payment] to perform witchcraft with other things. And this is what the prophet is saying: “For the sake of pieces of bread that they give you as your wages, you profaned My name among My people, in that you performed witchcraft on them for the prophets of Baal, to mislead My people.”

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:2:1.english: Even if he writes phylacteries with them - [the rest of the money] will also be preserved in his possession.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:3:1.hebrew: מאי קראה - דעל ידי דעבד בהו מצוה מיקיימי בידיה, דכתיב: "וידר ישראל וגו'". "והחרמתי" — לשון הקדש, ועל ידי כך נשמעת תפלתם ונפלו בידם:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:3:1.english: What is the verse - [That indicates] that by performing a mitzvah with them, they are preserved in his possession? As it is written: “And Israel vowed a vow...” (Numbers 21:2). “And I will consecrate” is an expression of consecration; and through this, their prayer was heard, and [their enemies] fell into their hands.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:4:1.english: And sleep of any amount - Either this [one] or that [one].

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:6:1.english: Rabbi Elai joined him - He drew near to the gentile.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:6:2.english: Mavgai is my name - That is my name.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:7:1.hebrew: אין מעבירין על האוכלין - המוצא אוכלין בדרך, אינו רשאי לעבור עליהן ולהניחן שם:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:7:1.english: One may not pass by food - One who finds food on the road is not permitted to pass by it and leave it there.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:8:1.hebrew: שהולכין אחרי רוב עוברי דרכים - מדלא שרא ליה לר' אלעאי למיכלינהו, דאחזקינהו בחזקת פיתן של נכרים, שרוב עוברי דרכים נכרים הן:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:8:1.english: That we follow the majority of travelers - From [the fact] that he did not permit Rabbi Ilai to eat them, as he held them under the presumption of bread of gentiles, for the majority of travelers are gentiles.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:8:2.english: That the leavened bread of a gentile - For [the incident] was after Passover.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:8:3.hebrew: מותר בהנאה - כגון הכא, דאיכא טובת הנאה לנכרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 64b:8:3.english: Permitted to benefit - Such as here, where there is the benefit of goodwill [in giving it] to the gentile.

Rashi on Eruvin 64b:9:1.english: To the one who was with him - To Rabbi Elai.

Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:16:1.hebrew: פותחין בחרטה - פי' בקונטרס: צריך לחכם למצוא פתח לשואל, שיהא לו פתחון פה לומר: "על דעת כן לא נדרתי, ואילו הייתי יודע שכן לא הייתי נודר", ונמצא נדר נעקר מאליו. "אין פותחין" — אין צריך לפתוח לו בחרטה, אלא החכם עוקר אע"פ שאינו מוצא לו טעם עקירה. ר"ג סבר כמ"ד פותחין, לפיכך הוצרך יישוב הדעת לחשב איזה פתח ימצא לו. ע"כ לשון הקונטרס. וקשיא לר"ת: דהא רב נחמן גופיה שמעינן ליה בהדיא בפרק ד' נדרים (נדרים דף כב:) דאמר: "הלכה פותחין בחרטה ונזקקין לאלהי ישראל", ובפ' נערה המאורסה (נדרים דף עז:) נקאמר רב נחמן: "הלכה נשאלין לנדרים מעומד, יחיד, ובלילה", ופריך עלה מהא דר"ג. וכתוב בכל הספרים: "ר"ג סבר אין פותחין בחרטה, למיעקר נדרא בעינן ובעי לעיוני, להכי ישב; ורב נחמן סבר פותחין בחרטה, ואפילו מעומד". אלא שיש ספרים שהגיהו איפכא על פי פירוש הקונטרס דהכא בשמעתא. ועוד, דאמר בסוף אלו מותרין (נדרים כ.): "בא מחמירין עליו דלא פתחינן ליה בחרטה" — משמע דאין פותחין היא חומרא! ועוד אמר בריש ד' נדרים (נדרים דף כא:) דרב הונא סבר פותחין בחרטה, מההוא דאתא לקמיה ואמר ליה "לבך עלך"; ורבה בר בר חנה דאמר ליה לההוא דאתא "אלו אתו י' בני אדם שיפייסוך", קסבר אין פותחין בחרטה. מפרש ר"ת: "פותחין בחרטה" היינו ששואלין אותו אם הוא מתחרט על מה שנדר, שאומר לו: "כדו תהית?", או "לבך עלך?", או "בעית נדר?" (שם), ושרינן ליה בהכי. ור"ג סבר אין פותחין להתיר לו בחרטה לחוד שמתחרט בו על מה שנדר, אלא צריך למצוא פתח לנדרו, כגון שאומר לו: "אילו באו עשרה בני אדם שיפייסוך", וכדפתח ר"ג לההוא טייעא, ששואלין אותו: "אדעתא דהכי נדרת?", שצריך לטרוח הרבה ולחשוב באיזה ענין ימצאו לו פתח לנדרו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:16:1.english: One opens with regret - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: It is necessary for the Sage to find an opening for the petitioner, so that he will have an opening of the mouth to say, "With such in mind I did not vow, and had I known that it was so, I would not have vowed," and the vow is found to be uprooted on its own. "[And the one who says] 'One does not open' [holds that] one does not need to open for him with regret; rather, the Sage uproots [the vow] even though he does not find a reason for uprooting for him. Rabban Gamliel held in accordance with the one who says 'one opens,' and therefore he required settledness of mind to calculate which opening he would find for him." Thus far is the language of the Kuntres. And Rabbeinu Tam found this difficult: For we explicitly heard Rav Nachman himself say in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Nedarim (Nedarim 22b): "The halakhah is that one opens with regret and attends to [vows made in the name of] the God of Israel." And in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah HaMeorasah (Nedarim 77b), Rav Nachman said: "The halakhah is that one may inquire about vows while standing, [before] an individual [expert], and at night," and [the Gemara] raises an objection against it from this [incident] of Rabban Gamliel. And it is written in all the books [i.e., manuscripts]: "Rabban Gamliel held that one does not open with regret; we require [a reason] to uproot the vow, and one needs to deliberate, and for this reason he sat down. And Rav Nachman held that one opens with regret, and [therefore it may be done] even while standing." However, there are books that emended [the text in Nedarim] to the opposite based on the commentary of the Kuntres here in [our] sugya. And furthermore, [the Gemara] says at the end of [the chapter entitled] Ellu Mutarin (Nedarim 20a): "[If] he comes [having intentionally taken a vow], one is stringent with him, that we do not open for him with regret" — which implies that "one does not open" is a stringency! And furthermore, [the Gemara] says at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Arba'ah Nedarim (Nedarim 21b) that Rav Huna held that one opens with regret, from that [incident of a man] who came before him and he said to him: "Is your heart upon you [i.e., do you regret it]?", whereas Rabba bar bar Chana, who said to that [man] who came: "Had ten men come to appease you [would you have vowed]?", held that one does not open with regret. Rabbeinu Tam explains: "One opens with regret" means that they ask him whether he regrets what he vowed, by saying to him: "Do you regret it now?", or "Is your heart upon you?", or "Do you still want the vow?" (ibid.), and we release him with that [alone]. And Rabban Gamliel held that one does not open to release him through regret alone, that he simply regrets what he vowed; rather, one must find an opening for his vow, such as saying to him: "Had ten men come to appease you [would you have vowed]?", and as Rabban Gamliel opened for that Arab, where they ask him: "Did you vow with this in mind?", which requires exerting much effort and thinking about in what manner they will find an opening for his vow.

Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:18:1.hebrew: כל הבוטה ראוי לדוקרו בחרב - בפרק ד' נדרים (נדרים דף כב.) אמר דלא פתחינן ליה בהא, דמתוך יראה יאמר: "אדעתא דהא לא נדר", אף על פי שמשקר. ועוד, פסקינן התם: הלכה פותחין בחרטה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:18:1.english: "Whoever utters [a vow] deserves to be pierced by a sword" - In the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Nedarim (Nedarim 22a), [the Gemara] says that we do not open [an opening for dissolution] for him with this [verse], for out of fear he will say, "It was not with this in mind that I vowed," even though he is lying. And furthermore, we rule there: The halakhah is that we open [dissolution] through regret.

Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:7:1.hebrew: שכוון רבן גמליאל ברוח הקדש - אע"פ שהיה שם זה רגיל באומות, כדאמרינן בפרק שני דמכות (דף יא.): "תמן אמרין: שכם נסיב, מבגאי גזר" — מכל מקום חשיב ליה כוונה ברוח הקדש. וההיא דסוף יבמות (דף קכב:) שאמר ליה: "יפה כוונת, שאריה שמי, כך קורין אותי בעירי" — לא שכוון אותו האיש ברוח הקדש, שלא קראו אריה אלא על שם כחו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:7:1.english: "That Rabban Gamliel divined by divine inspiration" - Even though this name was common among the nations, as we say in the second chapter of Makkot (11a): "There they say: Shechem married, [and] Mabgai was circumcised" — nevertheless, [the Gemara] considers it divining by divine inspiration. And that [incident] at the end of Yevamot (122b), where he said to him: "You divined well, for Aryeh is my name; that is what they call me in my town" — [it was] not that that man [who addressed him] divined by divine inspiration, for he called him "Aryeh" only on account of his strength.

Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:8:1.hebrew: שהולכין אחר רוב עוברי דרכים - כדפירש בקונטרס: מדלא שרי ליה לר' אלעאי למכלינהו, דאחזקינהו בחזקת פתן של נכרים, שרוב עוברי דרכים נכרים הם. דאם היינו תולין בשל ישראל — היה מותר, אף על פי שאחר הפסח היה בסמוך, דבישראל יש לומר: דאחר הפסח נעשה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:8:1.english: "That we follow the majority of travelers" - As explained in the Kuntres [Rashi]: From [the fact] that he did not permit Rabbi Elai to eat it, for he treated it under the presumption of [being] bread of gentiles, as the majority of travelers are gentiles. For if we were to attribute [it] to an Israelite, it would have been permitted, even though it was immediately after Passover, for in [the case of] an Israelite one can say that it was made after Passover.

Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:8:2.hebrew: ולמדנו שחמצו של עכו"ם אחר הפסח מותר בהנאה - מדנתנו לעכו"ם, דאיכא טובת הנאה דעכו"ם, כדפירש בקונטרס; דאי ס"ל דאסור בהנאה, היה לו לאסור מספק, דשמא בפסח נעשה. וא"ת: והיאך נתן ר"ג? והא דריש ר"י בסוף פ"ק דע"ז (דף כ.): "לא תחנם" — לא תתן להם מתנת חנם! ואע"ג דלעכו"ם המכירו שרי אפילו לר"י — דהא מוקמינן כר"י ההוא דשולח אדם ירך לעכו"ם בפסחים בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כב.), ותניא בתוספתא [דע"ז פ"ג]: "דאם היא שכינו מותר, מפני שהוא כמוכרו לו" — מ"מ הכא, הא אמרינן שלא היה מכירו רבן גמליאל מעולם! ויש לומר: דשמא לא סבר לה ר"ג להא דר"י. אי נמי, כיון שהיה העכו"ם מתלוה עמהן בדרך — שרי, דחשיב כמוכרו לו. והא דתניא בהניזקין (גיטין דף סא.): "מפרנסין עניי עכו"ם עם עניי ישראל מפני דרכי שלום" — ההיא נמי שרי משום דרכי שלום:
Tosafot on Eruvin 64b:8:2.english: "And we learned that leavened bread belonging to a gentile is permitted for benefit after Passover" - From [the fact] that he gave it to a gentile, for there is the gentile's favor [which is a benefit], as explained in the Kuntres; for if he maintained that it is forbidden to derive benefit [from a gentile's chametz after Passover], he should have forbidden it out of doubt, lest it was made on Passover. And if you say: But how could Rabban Gamliel give [it to him]? For doesn't Rabbi Yehuda expound at the end of the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (20a): "You shall not show them favor [lo techanem]" — do not give them a free gift? And even though [giving a gift] to a gentile whom he knows is permitted even according to Rabbi Yehuda — as we establish that [baraita which teaches] that a person may send a thigh [of meat] to a gentile in Pesachim, in the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 22a), [as being] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and it is taught in the Tosefta [Avodah Zarah, chapter 3]: that if he is his neighbor it is permitted, because it is as though he sells it to him — nevertheless, here, do we not say that Rabban Gamliel had never known him before? And one can say that perhaps Rabban Gamliel did not hold in accordance with this [exposition] of Rabbi Yehuda. Alternatively, since the gentile was accompanying them on the road, it is permitted, as he is considered like one who sells it to him. And [as for] that which is taught [in a baraita] in [the chapter entitled] HaNizakin (Gittin 61a): "We sustain the gentile poor along with the Jewish poor on account of the ways of peace" — that, too, is permitted because of the ways of peace.
